paper.title: SCI Officers & Servants Rules, 1961 — key points
paper.source: SCI Officers & Servants (Conditions of Service and Conduct) Rules, 1961

questions.stem: The Supreme Court Officers & Servants Rules, 1961 were framed under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 146 provides that appointments of officers and servants of the Supreme Court, and their conditions of service, are made by the Chief Justice of India by rules.

questions.stem: Under Article 146, appointments of officers and servants of the Supreme Court are made by:
options: the Secretary General of the Supreme Court
questions.explanation: Article 146 vests appointment power for officers and servants of the Court in the Chief Justice of India, with conditions of service prescribed by rules.

questions.stem: The SCI Officers & Servants Rules, 1961 consist of:
options: 49 rules in 5 Parts, with a Schedule
40 rules in 4 Parts, without a Schedule
questions.explanation: The Rules are short — 49 rules in 5 Parts (I General, II Strength/Appointment/Conditions, III Control and Discipline, IV Conduct, V Miscellaneous) plus a Schedule.

questions.stem: Which Part of the SCI Officers & Servants Rules, 1961 deals with conduct?
questions.explanation: Part IV (Rules 24–46) is the conduct code, covering intoxication, absence, gifts, private trade, relations with advocates, demonstrations and strikes, and so on.

questions.stem: Which rule of the SCI Officers & Servants Rules, 1961 lists the penalties?
questions.explanation: Rule 11 lists the penalties, distinguishing minor and major penalties. Rule 12 names the disciplinary authorities and Rule 13 the procedure for major penalties.

questions.stem: The procedure for imposing major penalties under the SCI Officers & Servants Rules, 1961 is prescribed by:
questions.explanation: Rule 13 prescribes the procedure for imposing major penalties; Rule 14 prescribes the procedure for minor penalties. This distinction is a favourite exam point.

questions.stem: The procedure for imposing minor penalties under the SCI Officers & Servants Rules, 1961 is prescribed by:
questions.explanation: Rule 14 prescribes the procedure for minor penalties, distinct from the major-penalty procedure in Rule 13.

questions.stem: Which Part of the SCI Officers & Servants Rules, 1961 governs control and discipline?
questions.explanation: Part III (Rules 10–23) governs control and discipline: penalties, disciplinary authorities, procedures, suspension, appeals and the Chief Justice's powers.

questions.stem: Under the SCI Officers & Servants Rules, 1961, the powers of control over Court servants reside with:
questions.explanation: Part III (Rules 10 and 23) vests control over Court servants in the Chief Justice of India, including powers in disciplinary matters.

questions.stem: Which rule of the SCI Officers & Servants Rules, 1961 deals with relations between Court servants and Advocates or Advocates on Record?
questions.explanation: Rule 39 regulates the relations of Court servants with Advocates or Advocates on Record — a rule unique to a court setting.

questions.stem: Rule 24A of the SCI Officers & Servants Rules, 1961 (inserted by amendment) deals with:
options: consumption of intoxicating drinks and drugs
questions.explanation: Rule 24A, inserted by amendment, governs the consumption of intoxicating drinks and drugs by Court servants.

questions.stem: Which Part of the SCI Officers & Servants Rules, 1961 deals with strength, appointment and conditions of service?
questions.explanation: Part II (Rules 3–9) covers strength and composition, method of recruitment, qualifications, appointing authority, probation, seniority and conditions of service.

questions.stem: The period of limitation for appeals under the SCI Officers & Servants Rules, 1961 is prescribed by:
questions.explanation: Rule 20 prescribes the period of limitation for appeals; Rule 21 deals with submission of appeals and Rule 22 with implementation of orders in appeal.

questions.stem: Under the SCI Officers & Servants Rules, 1961, the rule dealing with the care and preservation of Court property is:
questions.explanation: Rule 44 requires a Court servant to take due care of Court property and to prevent its damage or loss.

questions.stem: The SCI Officers & Servants Rules, 1961, as applicable, were amended up to:
questions.explanation: The consolidated version of the Rules reflects amendments up to 6 November 2024.

questions.stem: Suspension of a Court servant pending disciplinary proceedings under the SCI Officers & Servants Rules, 1961 is dealt with by:
questions.explanation: Rule 15 governs suspension pending disciplinary proceedings, while Rules 16 and 17 deal with Court servants on deputation.
